events.title: Sustainable Saturdays
events.description:
Join us for Sustainable Saturdays in partnership with Niagara Cares. Families can create art using recycled materials while exploring fun ways to reuse everyday items. Together, we’ll learn how small changes can help care for our community and the environment.
Included in museum admission. Space is limited! Book your tickets now.
*Members do not require a reservation.
*Events and dates are subject to change.
About the play partner: 
Niagara Cares is the heart of what we do and who we are at Niagara Bottling. For more than 60 years, we have been making a difference for our Team Members, consumers and communities through philanthropic giving, volunteering, water donations, and disaster relief. As a family-owned business, we are committed to creating meaningful change for our communities through a spirit of giving back both big and small. For more information, visitniagarawater.com/niagara-cares.
Frequently Asked Questions:
Is Sustainable Saturdays included with museum admission?
Yes. All Sustainable Saturdays activities are included with regular museum admission. 
When does Sustainable Saturdays take place?
Sustainable Saturdays is held on the fourth Saturday of every month in the Art Studio.

events.title: Author Kaelynn Partlow
events.description:
Kaelynn Partlow is an autistic therapist, public speaker, content creator, and author of Life on the Bridge. She shares autism insight through national speaking events, social media, and her work at Project Hope Foundation to promote real-world autism support and inclusion. She is best known for her appearance on the Netflix series Love on the Spectrum, where she became a recognizable and relatable voice for autism advocacy. Through her social media platforms, Kaelynn reaches millions with a message of meaningful inclusion, practical strategies, and systemic change.

Limited complimentary books available, while supplies last. 

No registration required, all ages welcome. Early arrival suggested.

Clifton C. Miller Community Center
300 Centennial Way
Tustin, CA 92780



This program is funded by support from the Samueli Foundation.

events.display_title: Meet the Author Food Tasting with Glenda Galván-García
events.description:
Join author and Executive Chef Glenda Galván-García for a special storytime inspired by La Enchilada Completa. Families will learn about the rich traditions of Mexican cuisine, enjoy a live guacamole demonstration and tasting, and explore how food brings people together. 
TIMES: 11am & 2:30pm
About the play partner: 
Glenda Galván-García is the Executive Chef at Granville’s award-winning restaurants in LA, as well as consultant for companies such as Mission Tortillas, Whole Foods, and Taco Bell. Proudly Chicana, she loves sharing principles of Mexican culture through food. The Whole Enchilada is her first foray into middle-grade literature. She lives in Orange County, CA.

events.title: Author Visit: Michelle Sterling
events.description:
Celebrate Filipino American Heritage Month at Tustin Library with a special author visit!

Michelle Sterling is an author, photographer and speech-language pathologist whose picture books include When Lola Visits, A Sweet New Year for Ren, and Maribel’s Year and Riding Through Rice Fields. Many of her stories are inspired by her heritage, family traditions and her love of gastronomy and food history. She lives in Southern California with her family.

Limited complimentary books available, while supplies last, courtesy of the Tustin Friends of the Library.

No registration required, all ages welcome. Early arrival suggested.

For more information, call 714-544-7725 or email ocpl.tustin@occr.ocgov.com
